changelog: Insert a context-limited principle preventing rightward shifts into short complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases in dense/short-latency contexts — addresses the primary finding that the prompt over-corrects by pushing cuts into short multiword names or complements and so harms cohesion (evidence: en_us_651, en_us_1527, en_us_1137).
Replace C8 to address the primary finding: make the principle explicitly prefer keeping multiword names and short noun phrases intact in dense/short-latency settings.
Delete E2, E3, E4, E7, E8, E9, E10, E12, E13 — remove nine large examples to meet the size budget and the 'at most 8 examples' constraint; kept a representative small set of worked cases.

Replace the four handcrafted example units with measured, labeled examples that illustrate the primary finding (cuts pushed rightward into short complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases in dense/low-latency contexts). This gives scorers worked cases directly showing the failure modes (en_us_651, en_us_1137) and additional short-latency instances (en_us_1118, en_us_767).
Edits obey the 'examples_only' constraint and do not change any Core Principles, so the change is traceable to the diagnosis about over-correction into short multiword names/complements.

Replace C6 to add a concise, targeted principle that in dense/short-latency contexts scorers should avoid shifting cuts rightward into short complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases; this directly addresses the primary finding about over-correction that harms cohesion.
